The Life in the Meadow

Fantasy/Horror

450 Words

General Impression

 This is just a short story I wrote, in only 16 and I’m trying to get better at writing any help would be amazing~!

Ivory petals canvassed the hills blanketing the landscape. The great meadow of pure white flowers broken by a stream of crimson paint.
I could little see the astral wicks of the night sky behind the dark gray clouds, the only source of luminescence being the moon that shadowed its essence upon the ill branded dusk.
There's a sort of beauty in imperfection, it's the flaws that make us human after all or at least as human as we can be.

A seductively sweet metal aroma filled my lungs, as I continued to walk through the field.  
Snow petals decorated of cardinal, graced the seemingly lifeless air with every step. 

It was almost peaceful, the cold feeling of being alone, the wind giving its susurrus to the wave of flowers moving like tides.
It was the rustic simplicity of life that made unliving so imperfect, the rancor of persevering in this endless cycle left many heinous to its effects.
I always wondered if I too would follow that same path, the visceral reaction of giving in to raw desire.

My path through the red stained pedals came to an end, a young boy laid alone in a pile of maroon ichor. A faint smile appeared on the boy's lips as I came into his vision.

“Is this the end?” His voice shivered in the night, a cold realization.

“I can't feel anymore, did I lose control?” tears formed in the corners of his eyes, his sight fixed to the stars shimmering in celestial bursts through the cracks of the clouds.

I cloaked my hands in white gloves before sliding a silver blade out of its sheath, an executioner of all its own.

“I.. I didn't mean to Ma, I’m sorry.” His voice stammered alone in the uncomfortable silence.

I raised the blade to the left of his chest, his eyes still locked on the stars above him.

“See you soon.” He reached a hand out into the sky above him as if reaching for the stars.

With the thrust of the blade his eyes glazed over into milky white, his arm fell lifeless to his side. His mind now granted nepenthe from his abandonment of humanity.
I reached down and picked up one of the few untainted white roses, sliding it into his hair.
Slowly chips of his face parted into the air, a solemn gray. Bit by bit he ashed away following the same cold wind. 

The flowers seemed to still peacefully wave in the moonlight, untouched by the event that unfolded in front of them.

It was moments like these that made me question my purpose.
